business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Document Automation and E-Signature Authentication

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–European Union Free Trade Agreement (provisionally effective 2013)
Colombia–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. incorporation regime); Ley 526 de 1999 as amended by Ley 1121 de 2006 (UIAF AML/CFT framework); Ley 1762 de 2015 (AML aggravations); Ley 2195 de 2022, Art. 76 (beneficiario final corporate registry mandate); Decreto 2555 de 2010 (AML/CFT regulatory architecture); Circular Básica Jurídica de la Superintendencia de Sociedades (Capítulo X – SAGRILAFT); official UBO reporting platform ORBE.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation of each non-resident corporate shareholder (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial or equivalent registry authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the origin state is not a Party to the Apostille Convention, full Consular Legalization at the Colombian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney for company incorporation executed by non-resident shareholders and final beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by certified Spanish translation by a registered official translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports/national identity documents of all non-resident shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or competent civil registry authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; passport copies must be certified and translated

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO and PEP exposure affidavit (Declaración jurada de beneficiario final y vinculación a PEP)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin (or Colombian notary if executed domestically)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (foreign execution) or domestic notarial acknowledgement (Colombian execution)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based SAGRILAFT screening before incorporation: (i) PEP identification against UIAF and Superintendencia Financiera public lists; (ii) OFAC SDN, UN Security Council Consolidated List, and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iii) Colombian national judicial and tax records; (iv) 25% ownership and control-threshold UBO re-verification, refreshed within 90 days of any ownership change and continuously monitored under Decreto 2555 de 2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial (www.rues.org.co), administered through the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá via www.ccb.org.co) for the homonimia (name availability) certificate
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate denomination may include Spanish, Latin, or foreign-language expressions customarily accepted in Colombian commerce; wholly English or non-Spanish names are admitted only if accompanied by a Spanish descriptive transliteration or commercial explanation. The registered name must conclude with the 'S.A.S.' sigla or otherwise explicitly identify the simplified stock company form under Ley 1258 de 2008, Art. 2 and Código de Comercio, Art. 58.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is not statutorily extendable; the applicant must obtain a fresh homonimia certificate if the 30-day window lapses. Upon rejection, the incorporator may file a 'recurso de reconsideración' before the issuing Cámara de Comercio within 10 working days of notification under Ley 1437 de 2011 (CPACA), attaching a revised denomination; if denied, a 'recurso de apelación' may be filed with the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the same 10-working-day term. An alternative name clearance run may be initiated in parallel without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk LegalTech SaaS only where the declared domicile is a verifiable physical address inside the municipal jurisdiction of the Cámara de Comercio and is capable of receiving judicial and administrative notifications. Co-working and managed-office addresses are accepted; pure virtual-mailbox operators without a Colombian physical footprint are not accepted for S.A.S. registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 5–8% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first 24 months, based on the low-risk AML tier, administrative consistency of a co-working address, and complete SAGRILAFT documentation for a digital services entity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Homonimia name availability certificate (certificado de homonimia) for the proposed S.A.S. denomination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (via RUES)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff schedule issued by Confecámaras

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial acknowledgement of signatures on the private incorporation document (reconocimiento de firmas)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff schedule of the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mercantile registration and filing of the incorporation document (matrícula mercantil) of the S.A.S.
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on declared subscribed capital (estimated COP 1,000,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille of the foreign parent company's certificate of existence and legal representation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the shareholder's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing statutory apostille fee in the origin jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of apostilled corporate, notarial, and identity documents
UBO / Beneficiario Final registration through the ORBE platform (including preparation of the UBO disclosure matrix)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration without fee; preparation covered by counsel line item below

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: DIAN RUT (Registro Único Tributario) pre-assignment for the S.A.S.
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel — pre-incorporation due diligence, SAGRILAFT/UBO profiling, bylaw drafting, and regulatory filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed fee for standard low-risk S.A.S. incorporation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and EU consolidated sanctions screening platform — one-year license for initial and continuous UBO/PEPS verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk legal-tech corporate customer onboarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for public deed (escritura pública) protocol in the event that in-kind contributions or real-property contributions are later identified
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff; contingency only, not charged if private-document route is finalized

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (arts. 1-50) – S.A.S. regime; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971) arts. 110-125 (mercantile registration) and 373-381 (corporate books); Decreto 1074 de 2015 arts. 2.2.2.33.1 et seq. (RUES integration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – Registro Único Empresarial (RUES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Estatutos) inscribed in the Registro Mercantil; attested by the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Ley 1258/2008; capital freely set in the charter; at least one subscribed and paid share per founding shareholder; in-kind contributions require sworn appraisal; no escrow account or consignment requirement for cash contributions
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, First, that the subscribed share capital specified in the incorporation contract is accepted, the shares are duly subscribed and paid within the statutory term by the founding shareholders, and the shareholder register is opened. Second, the registered office is fixed at the address declared to the Chamber of Commerce, and the legal representative is authorized to present the formation instrument to RUES. Third, the following officers are appointed: Gerente, who shall hold the broadest representation powers to open bank accounts and execute legal-tech subscription agreements, and Secretario General for corporate minutes. Fourth, the board directs the registration of the NIT before DIAN, compliance with municipal commercial registration, and the adoption of the corporate books, ratifying this first constitutional act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Confirmation and Homonymy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (CCB) – online name search portal and in-person branch windows
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name search request through the CCB virtual platform; obtain the certificado de homonimia evidencing that the proposed denomination (e.g., '[CLIENT] LegalTech S.A.S.') is not identical to any registered company name; the certificate is valid for 90 days; the charter must reserve the name before final filing.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the requesting incorporator
Completed homonymy application form
Draft bylaws indicating the proposed corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an identical or confusingly similar name is detected, submit a second and third alternative denomination; if the application is wrongly rejected, interpose a reconsideration petition before the CCB Legal Representative within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Legalization of the S.A.S. Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders in private instrument (notarial deed only when real property is contributed); later certified by CCB
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the private incorporation contract (estatutos) before two witnesses, including: company name, domicile, corporate purpose, term, capital and share classes, reserved governance matters, administrator appointment, and arbitration clauses; if non-cash contributions are made, attach a sworn inventory and appraisal of each asset; the instrument must be dated and signed by all shareholders.
required_dossiers: Final bylaws draft
National ID or passport of each shareholder
Power of attorney if signing through an agent
Sworn statement of subscription and payment schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute a clarificatory addendum (reforma estatutaria) in the same solemnity before registry filing to cure omissions; any rectification made pre-inscription carries no penalty fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registry Fees and Regional Registration Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CCB treasury windows and PSE online payment platform; Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda for the Impuesto de Registro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the mercantile registration fee based on the declared capital and pay the inscription tariff; in Bogotá, the regional registration tax (Impuesto de Registro) is assessed at 0.7% of the capital amount subject to the statutory floor; upload the payment receipt to the RUES enrolment flow and conserve the liquidation voucher as proof.
required_dossiers: Executed bylaws and homonymy certificate
RUT provisional (if already obtained)
PSE receipt or credit card payment voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tariff is overcharged, request a refund via the CCB 'Devolución de Pagos' procedure; if underpaid, CCB issues a complementary liquidation with a 10% surcharge that must be settled within 10 business days before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Company and Matrícula Mercantil in the RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – Registro Mercantil / RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed charter, the internal RUES registration form, the homonymy certificate and proof of fee payment; upon qualification, the CCB issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal , which is the sole evidence of legal existence; the legal representative and substitute representatives are simultaneously inscribed in the same record.
required_dossiers: Original executed incorporation contract
Certificado de homonimia
RUES standard inscription form
Proof of tariff and tax payment
Copy of the legal representative's identity document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry officer issues formal observations (devolución del trámite), cure the observations within the 10-day statutory term and resubmit the corrected file without additional registry tariff; persistent defects may be appealed before the CCB internal appellate body.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NIT and RUT Formalization before DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (MUISCA online portal and assistance desks)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUT pre-registration via MUISCA using the legal representative's digital identity; declare the mandatory tax obligations (corporate income tax, ICA, withholdings, VAT for digital services, and e-invoicing flag); obtain the definitive NIT and issue the RUT printout; register the final beneficiary information in the same transaction where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued within the last 30 days
Legal representative's cédula or passport
Office lease agreement proving the registered address
Corporate email and mobile number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT filing is rejected for registry data mismatch, present the updated CCB certificate and resubmit the electronic form; formal objections may be raised through the recurso de reposición before DIAN within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, E-Invoicing and Beneficial Owner Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks supervised by Superintendencia Financiera; DIAN for facturación electrónica; RUES/DIAN for beneficial ownership registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account for Stripe and credit card payouts; certify the Gerente as sole signatory with a recent board resolution; (ii) activate the e-invoicing software provider at DIAN and issue the first credit note; (iii) file the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales if any natural person directly or indirectly holds more than 5% capital or exercises control.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
NIT and RUT
Bylaws and signatory appointment resolution
Passport or ID of beneficial owners
Proof of registered address and utility bill
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC queries, provide the standard S.A.S. compliance pack and re-file the application; unwarranted refusal may be reported to the Defensor del Consumidor Financiero or the Superintendencia Financiera for remedial instruction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) – Delegatura de Supervisión de Entidades de Certificación Digital; Secretaría Distrital de Planeación for land-use certification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating license required for pure cloud software and e-signature platform deployment; voluntary accreditation as 'Entidad de Certificación Digital Abierta' under Law 527/1999 and Decree 2364/2012 only if issuing proprietary digital certificates; mandatory Certificado de Uso del Suelo (LURB) for the office premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: ANLA – Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales; Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (Bogotá) for local urban operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EXEMPT – no EIA required; software/SaaS activity generates no point-source industrial emissions; only municipal environmental certificate and solid-waste hauler registration apply under Decree 1076/2015 art. 2.2.2.3.2
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic sanitary wastewater only to municipal sewer per Resolución 0631/2015 non-industrial limits; zero VOC or industrial discharge; electronic waste (RAEE) management per Ley 1672/2013 and Resolución 1512/2010; ordinary solid waste through authorized public utility

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Annual fire-safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos (Certificado de Bomberos); SG-SST occupational health and safety plan per Resolución 0312 de 2019 (standard level, minimal cycle for under 10 employees); ARL affiliation for labor-risk coverage; structural and occupancy certificate from the local curaduría verifying seismic load safety for the contracted office floor

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - Official portal: www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities without a permanent establishment must obtain a Tax Identification Number (NIT) through the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) by appointing a local fiscal agent or attorney-in-fact. Registration is completed electronically via DIAN's user portal using a digital signature certificate issued in Colombia, followed by formal filing of the RUT and issuance of the NIT certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available. A Colombian S.A.S. is subject to entity-level corporate income tax. The only relevant statutory election, where eligible, is the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE), which permits a combined taxation regime for qualifying small-service entities with annual gross revenue below statutory thresholds. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized as a separate mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None (zero de minimis threshold). Any person or foreign digital service provider making taxable supplies of services to Colombia, or entering into export activities, must register for VAT through the RUT process; non-resident digital suppliers have no fiscal turnover threshold triggering registration for services used in Colombia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica de Venta - FEV) applies. Invoices must be generated by DIAN-authorized software, contain the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) stamp, and be transmitted to DIAN in near-real time through government web-service APIs. Digital fiscal clearance is effected via DIAN online validation; export invoices also require electronic validation and the exporter's digital certificate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Services (including LegalTech SaaS, cloud document automation, and e-signature authentication) qualify for the VAT 0% rate where the recipient is a non-resident entity with no domicile in Colombia, the service is effectively used or exploited abroad, and the supplier documents the export nature in compliance with Article 481 of the Colombian Tax Statute and DIAN interpretative rules. For digital services, the zero-rating applies only if the sale is not rendered for direct use within Colombia and the contract indicates offshore usage.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Invoice (Factura de Venta Electrónica) marked with VAT 0% export status
Signed service contract or order documentation indicating overseas recipient and offshore use
Foreign Exchange Declaration (Declaración de Cambio) for export services
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reembolso de Divisas) issued by the Colombian bank or FX intermediary
Certified proof of non-resident status of the counterparty (e.g., tax domicile certificate) and CUFE-validated electronic export invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to documentary audit by DIAN. If the export status is successfully challenged, the VAT becomes payable at 19% on the full invoice value, plus inflation-adjusted default interest and a penalty generally equivalent to 100–200% of the omitted tax where inaccuracy is attributed to negligence or fraud. Submission of forged export documents may trigger criminal liability for fraud under Colombian tax and criminal law, including imprisonment, and retrospective clawback of any VAT refunds received.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), acting with DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) as enforcement authority, pursuant to Resolución Externa 8 de 2000 and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83 (Régimen Cambiario). The Junta Directiva del Banco de la República issues all foreign-exchange control regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a free-market foreign-exchange regime (Régimen de Libre Cambio) under Ley 9 de 1991. Current-account operations, including service-export receipts and profit remittances, are fully convertible and freely negotiable through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries (IMCs) without prior Central Bank authorization. Capital-account operations, including non-resident equity injections into a S.A.S., are freely convertible but subject to mandatory registration with Banco de la República (Registro de Inversión Internacional). Profit remittance hurdles are documentary only: proof of registered foreign-investment status, DIAN tax-compliance filings, dividend-distribution minutes, applicable dividend withholding at the statutory rate for non-resident shareholders on distributed taxed profits, and execution through an IMC. Compliance is declaratory and ex-post; no PRIOR approval is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export receipts—including software-as-a-service licensing fees under ISIC 6201—equal to or exceeding the USD 10,000 equivalent must be collected and channeled (canalizado) through the Colombian foreign-exchange market via an authorized IMC within six (6) months from the date of service performance or the corresponding receivable due date. The mandatory conversion (surrender) ratio is 100%: the exporter must sell the hard-currency proceeds to the IMC for local COP, or place them in a permitted foreign-currency account maintained with the IMC under the exchange regime. Receipts below the USD 10,000 threshold remain un-intermediated and may be collected freely. Under-reporting, late canalización, or split structuring near the threshold creates remedial fines, DIAN recategorization risk, and loss of export-benefit eligibility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (COP plus USD collection sweeps); Capital Escrow/Investment Settlement Account (Cuenta de Inversión Extranjera)
Operational Account; Capital Escrow/Investment Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-to-Medium as a treasury substitute; Medium as a supplementary collection rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Mercury or Wise, holding no Colombian financial license, cannot qualify as IMCs under Colombian FX law; they cannot on-ramp COP disbursements, cannot execute local payroll, cannot enter Colombian forward contracts, and cannot perform the statutory canalización of export proceeds of USD 10,000 or more. They may lawfully hold USD/EUR SaaS collections as offshore receivables and consolidate funds before a single SWIFT MT103 transfer into the Colombian IMC account. Any EMI collecting funds for a Colombian exporter must final-settle through the IMC channel within the six-month statutory window.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and an in-person signature-registration interview are mandatory in practice: the S.A.S. legal representative and the controlling signatories must appear at the bank branch (or before a Colombian notary or Colombian consulate when executing powers of attorney) to register the dual-signature mandate. Remote account opening is available only to qualifying established clients using certified digital signature (firma electrónica certificada) and apostilled corporate documents. A newly incorporated S.A.S. with wholly non-resident ownership and no prior local banking relationship will uniformly face: in-person onboarding, notarized board minutes appointing the legal representative, a live sworn source-of-funds interview, and presentation of the company's actual corporate charter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO ownership and fully remote management of a digital-only SaaS business lacking physical commercial premises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificado de Cámara de Comercio issued within 90 days showing the share registry; apostilled and notarized bylaws (certificado de existencia y representación legal); passports and national ID of all directors and 5% or greater UBOs; UBO declaration registered with DIAN under the Beneficiario Final regime; executed SaaS subscription agreements and master services contracts; Stripe settlement reports and corresponding bank statements proving genuine cross-border revenue; physical shareholder residence evidence; and current tax-compliance certificates (RUT, Form 260/240).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or late registration of the non-resident capital injection with Banco de la República, flagged by the bank at settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Banco de la República Registro de Inversión Internacional certificate or platform acknowledgment filed within the legal term; IMC settlement confirmation slips; board minutes and shareholders' resolution authorizing the capital increase under Ley 1258 de 2008; source-of-funds documentation from the non-resident investor (bank statements, corporate board minutes, intercompany resolutions).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ODD flags on recurring outbound disbursements to group entities and technology offshoring vendors in lower-tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer-pricing documentation with a four-year comparability study; signed intercompany service agreements with deliverables and milestone evidence; downstream subcontractor agreements; DIAN withholding tax certificates (Rete-Renta and Rete-IVA); liquidated invoices for services performed; business rationale narrative; and FATF-aligned purpose descriptions for each recurring beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX red flags on split settlements, near-threshold USD 9,999 wire structuring, or delayed canalización of export proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury discipline calendar pairing invoices with SWIFT MT103 evidence; certified IMC FX confirmation slips showing each canalización event within the six-month term; a board-approved treasury FX policy committing to 100% channeling of export proceeds through the IMC; compliance officer records; external auditor confirmation; and regulator correspondence for any exceptional handling.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant sequence: (1) Shareholders and board approve the non-resident equity contribution to the S.A.S.; (2) investor sends a SWIFT MT103 into the designated local IMC repository account, beneficiary name of the S.A.S., referencing the Banco de la República Foreign Investment Registry unique identifier; (3) the IMC converts the hard-currency receipt into COP under the foreign-investment purpose code (Declaración de Cambio, Part I, concept: Inversión Extranjera Directa / Aportes al capital); (4) the S.A.S. files the Registro de Inversión Internacional with Banco de la República within the legal deadline; (5) corporate formalities are completed by inscribing the capital increase with the Cámara de Comercio. Any mixed equity and intercompany-loan injection must be split into separate MT103 transfers with distinct purpose codes to prevent DIAN and Banco de la República reclassification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor payments under business-services purpose codes. For high-value trade settlement, an irrevocable confirmed commercial letter of credit under UCP600 is routed through the local IMC bank as issuing or confirming bank, using the MT700/MTA/MT799 message sequence for issuance, amendments, negotiation, and acceptance. Domestic COP disbursements clear through the Colombian electronic clearing house (Cámara de Compensación Electrónica / CUD) on a T+0 or T+1 cycle, with the IMC bank acting as the initiating member. Intra-group treasury transfers use the MT101 client-transfer instruction into foreign IMC beneficiary accounts. Every outbound MT103 must carry the S.A.S. RUT tax ID, beneficiary name with OFAC-consistent references, and a purpose-of-payment code aligned with DIAN and Banco de la República declaration requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD plain-vanilla deliverable forwards (contratos a término) executed through an IMC or regulated dealer, reserved for current-account commercial flows and underlying subscription invoices, net-exposure basis only

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on COP/USD and COP/EUR referencing the Colombian TRM (tasa representativa del mercado), cash-settled in USD or EUR, permitted for hedging projected SaaS collections and intercompany receivables

Onshore FX swaps (swap de liquidez) between COP and hard currency across one- and three-month tenors through local IMC counterparties, used to reposition liquidity between escrow and operational accounts

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) linking USD-denominated intercompany funding or bonded debt to COP corporate liabilities, subject to Banco de la República registration and mark-to-market COP-hedging compliance

Option-based zero-cost collars and binary-neutral structures available through specialized Colombian broker-dealers but restricted to documented transactional exposure; speculative overlay is prohibited under the Régimen Cambiario and not recommended at this stage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (annual commercial registration renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the company's domicile (Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 31 March each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Chamber may charge arrears, interest, and fines after 31 March; prolonged non-renewal can cause the Chamber to inactivate or administratively cancel the registration, preventing the company from obtaining commercial certificates and lawfully operating.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Acta de Asamblea General de Accionistas approving annual financial statements and informe de gestión
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Registro Mercantil) if registration of the corporate minutes is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the 31 December fiscal year-end, i.e. no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the assembly and register the act may invalidate profit distributions, prevent registration of corporate acts, and expose the legal representative to fines; the Revisor Fiscal, if any, must report non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (annual corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the DIAN date assigned to the taxpayer's NIT ending; generally between mid-April and the end of June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to 5% of the tax in charge, plus daily arrears interest; continued default may lead to NIT suspension and compulsory collection, but does not by itself trigger administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: S.A.S. must appoint a Revisor Fiscal when at 31 December of the prior year gross assets are equal to or exceed 5,000 SMMLV, or gross income equals or exceeds 3,000 SMMLV, or when required by the bylaws or by law; otherwise an independent statutory audit is not mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia under Law 1314 of 2009; most S.A.S. apply IFRS for SMEs (Grupo 2); full IFRS applies to Grupo 1 entities; financial statements are prepared in COP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must file and annually confirm its final beneficiary owner(s) in DIAN's Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF), even if there is no ownership change; share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the annual confirmation, with updates according to DIAN's calendar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–900 per year for local registered-office and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800–6,500 per year for a small/mid-size S.A.S. when a Revisor Fiscal is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Colombian SAS entities are subject to a headline 35% CIT rate. Qualifying software/creative companies may access the orange-economy rent exemption (exención de economía naranja, Article 235-2 ET) for up to 7-10 years, and exporters of technology services/SaaS may rely on the services-export rent exemption under Article 235-2 ET if the recipient is a foreign non-branch entity. The DIAN also permits accelerated depreciation and tax credits for certain innovation investments. Free Trade Zone residents obtain a 20% CIT rate; after all incentives, early-stage LegalTech SaaS can achieve an effective cash rate below the statutory 35% while the exemption window lasts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios, filed electronically through the DIAN Muisca (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicios y Trámites Control) portal using the taxpayer's NIT and digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return is due between the 9th day of the fourth month and the 7th day of the sixth month following the fiscal year-end. The exact date is set by DIAN by resolution according to the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT; failing that date triggers penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique taxpayer ID, legal type identifier (SAS), tax status code and social reason.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian SAS is a domestic income tax resident solely by incorporation. The foreign shareholders do not file Form 110; the Colombian entity itself reports under its own NIT regardless of foreign ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary and secondary ISIC economic activity codes as registered in the RUT. For this scope, code 6201 must be present.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the RUT reflects the actual LegalTech/SaaS activity. Non-resident investors must not cause the entity to mis-declare its activity code; inconsistency is a common DIAN red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from software subscriptions, e-signature fees, recurring SaaS contracts, and ancillary digital services, before costs and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All amounts must be converted to COP using the tax-month exchange rate certified by DIAN. Cross-border SaaS revenue sourced to Colombia is reportable; foreign-to-foreign resale structures do not eliminate the SAS filing duty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs, cloud hosting, infrastructure, personnel, subcontracting, third-party API fees, legal/accounting expenses, and amortization of software development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties for cloud/AI or software development must be tested under the transfer-pricing standard and supported by contemporaneous documentation. They must be arm's-length and commercially rational.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net ordinary profit after costs and deductible expenses, before loss compensation and exempt-income deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot deduct intercompany charges that lack economic substance or are not supported by dated contracts and invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses available under the 12-year carryforward regime, offset subject to the statutory rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses generated by a shell arrangement or artificial intra-group allocation may be challenged. Only real Colombian operating losses may be carried forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after loss offsets, exempt income, and exclusion of non-taxable revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The DIAN will audit this figure against revenue data, bank flows, Stripe/credit-card settlement reports, and the Form 110 prior-year numbers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computed at the 35% rate on the taxable base, plus any complementary taxes or surcharges applicable to the taxpayer's status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even if the foreign parent is taxable abroad, the Colombian entity cannot reduce its taxable income below the DIAN-determined base without a legal exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes withheld at source from customers, prior-year advance payments, withholding tax credits, and CREE/imporrenta credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit is available for Colombian-source withholding only; foreign taxes paid by the parent in its own jurisdiction are not creditable on the domestic SAS return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 115 - Saldo a favor o saldo a pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability after credits. If a refund (saldo a favor) is claimed, an official DIAN

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an extemporaneous-return penalty equal to 5% of the tax payable for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due, with a minimum penalty of 10 UVT if no tax is due. Late payment accrues monthly moratory interest at the DIAN rate. An inexact or false return attracts a 100% penalty on the understated tax difference. Repeated non-filing allows DIAN to assess the tax ex officio using presumptive methods and to impose criminal tax-evasion sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% for dividends paid out of profits not already subject to CIT at the corporate level; 10% on dividends distributed from profits already taxed in Colombia. In practice, a dividend paid by a Colombian SAS to a foreign shareholder is subject to withholding at the applicable statutory rate, and the payor must remit the tax through Form 110 and the relevant DIAN collection forms.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a lower DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the competent authority of its jurisdiction of residence, apostille or legalize it, provide a Spanish translation if required, and submit the TRC plus a beneficial-ownership/LOB declaration to the Colombian withholding agent before the payment is processed. The withholding agent must retain the evidence and report the treaty-protected payment. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident must file a refund claim before the DIAN within the statutory limitation period, attaching the TRC, payment vouchers, and supporting contracts.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are generally 15% for royalties paid to foreign beneficiaries and 15% for interest paid abroad, with possible higher rates for back-to-back or related-party financing. DTA rates for royalties and interest commonly range from 0% to 15%, depending on the treaty. Each reduced-rate claim requires a TRC and compliance with the Colombian controlled-foreign-company and debt-equity thin-capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For FY2024, the Local File and Master File obligations arise for taxpayers with gross income or total assets exceeding approximately COP 4,706,000,000 (100,000 UVT of COP 47,065), or for related-party cross-border transactions exceeding approximately COP 470,000,000 (10,000 UVT). The Master File is also required when the multinational group has consolidated turnover exceeding COP 75,000,000,000. The annual TP informative return (Form 120) must be filed electronically when the same thresholds are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulation comparable to the UAE ESR. Instead, the DIAN applies substance-over-form, commercial-rationality, and general anti-abuse principles under the Tax Code and the DTA Principal Purpose Test. A Colombian SAS engaged in LegalTech SaaS must maintain real personnel, an operational office or hub, substantive software contracts, active bank accounts, board minutes, and business decision-making in Colombia in order to support ordinary CIT treatment, TP comparisons, and treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False or Inexact CIT Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting SaaS subscription revenue, fabricating cloud invoices, classifying non-deductible distributions as costs, or undervaluing cross-border related-party contracts to reduce the 35% CIT base while filing Form 110.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty under Article 647 ET equal to 100% of the omitted or understated tax, plus moratory interest. Criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment of 48 to 108 months and fines under Law 1778/2016 Article 434A. The entity also faces exclusion from tax amnesties and inability to obtain clean tax certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who sign the false return are jointly and severally liable for the tax, interest, and penalties under Article 794 ET. Where the evasion is proven as deliberate fraud, the corporate veil is pierced; directors face imprisonment, travel bans, asset embargo, prohibitions on serving as officer/manager of Colombian companies, and civil restitution to the DIAN and investors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / Late Filing / TP Documentation Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the Form 110 or Form 120 deadlines, omitting the Local File, refusing to produce contemporaneous TP documentation, or failing to remit withholding taxes on payments to non-resident shareholders and vendors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of 5% per month of the tax payable, capped at 100%; sanction for overdue TP documentation may be a percentage of the affected transaction value or a fixed UVT-based fine. DIAN can issue an ex officio assessment based on presumptive income, and the absence of TP documentation shifts the burden to the taxpayer. Criminal sanctions apply if the default is linked to evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative is personally liable for withholding taxes not remitted to the DIAN. Travel restraints, bank account freezes, and enforcement against personal assets may be ordered for persistent non-compliance. Directors who knowingly fail to disclose related-party transactions may face personal fines and criminal prosecution for aiding tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Transactions / Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SAS with no employees, no office, no operating contracts, no client-facing substance, or interposing it solely to channel royalties and dividends to a lower-tax jurisdiction or to access DTA relief that the ultimate beneficial owner could not access directly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN will disregard the corporate form, recharacterize the structure, deny treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test, and apply the full statutory WHT of up to 35% on dividends and applicable rates on royalties/interest, plus penalties and moratory interest. The transactions may also be treated as inexact entries, attracting a 100% inexactness penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute simulated back-to-back agreements, phantom employment contracts, or circular funding structures are treated as parties to tax fraud; they may be held civilly liable for the full tax deficiency and face criminal indictment, veil-piercing, asset confiscation, and a ban on international travel pending criminal tax proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting customer settlement funds through Stripe or credit-card rails without basic KYC/CDD procedures, collecting proceeds from anonymous digital-wallet accounts, processing payments for transactions that are not evidenced by valid SaaS contracts, or funneling invoice payments to offshore accounts without commercial explanation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Colombian AML/FT legislation (Law 526/2012 and Decree 83/2017) imposes administrative fines on companies that fail to identify final beneficiaries or file suspicious-transaction reports with the UIAF. The fines can reach thousands of UVT, and if the underlying activity facilitates money laundering, the responsible parties face up to 20 years of imprisonment. Non-compliance also renders tax refunds and treaty benefits unavailable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who approve or ignore irregular payment flows are personally liable for AML fines, may be excluded from managing financial or corporate entities, and can suffer preventive personal measure, including travel bans, asset seizures, and pretrial detention. The corporate limited-liability shield does not protect managers who knowingly participate in laundering proceeds derived from tax fraud.
